newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PolyGram H1 net seen up modestly.
newsitem.headline: PolyGram H1 net seen up modestly.

text.p: Music and entertainment group PolyGram NV is set to report a small gain in first half 1997 net profit next Tuesday, with a solid music performance again offset by operating losses from film, analysts said on Wednesday.
Analysts see the company, 75-percent owned by Philips Electronics NV, announcing a net profit of 275-286 million guilders, against 272 million in the first half of 1996.

"We're going for a small increase, music is better but there will be a loss in film," said David Chermont of Merrill Lynch. Analysts anticipate second quarter operating losses in film will match the 55 million booked in the first quarter.
PolyGram's first quarter net profit slipped to 122 million guilders from 124 million, hurt by underperformance of the films "Portrait of a Lady" and "Gridlock'd".

PolyGram chief executive Alain Levy has said the film unit -- which ended 1996 with an operating loss of 35 million guilders after inching into profit in the second half -- was not expected to make a profit this year.
Strong releases from Irish rock band U2 and teenage pop group Hanson, which have both performed strongly in the album charts, should keep the music side ticking over, say analysts.

"The Hanson album is doing well for PolyGram just about everywhere, certainly in the U.S. The last I heard it had sold something like three million copies. If Hanson has got some durability that will be good news for them," an analyst said.

"The U2 album has done well but maybe not as well as they would have liked at over five million. That's been a bit of a problem... the lack of big selling albums," said the analyst who declined to be named.

PolyGram's movie operation is seen performing better later in the year after the expected release of potentially big money spinners including "The Game", starring Michael Douglas and "The Big Lebowski", with Jeff Bridges.
Another new movie, the comedy "Bean", on release in Australia and the Netherlands, is seen performing strongly and adding to film's performance in the third quarter.

"The film Bean has started well in Australia. I get the impression that the whole of continental Europe can't wait for it to come out, it's very popular. The Dutch are opening it on a record number of screens, for instance," said the analyst.
Chermont said PolyGram should also benefit from currency impacts, with the guilder continuing weak against a number of currencies, including the dollar and the pound.
"Currencies will have an important impact on the figures," he said, declining to be more specific.
